title: Normal saline in hypovolemic shock raises preload: increased end-diastolic sarcomere length
vignette: A 43-year-old man comes to the emergency department after experiencing 4 episodes of coffee ground emesis that started earlier this morning. He also describes epigastric pain over the last 3-4 months that was relieved by over-the-counter antacids. He has no other past medical history. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the last 20 years but does not use alcohol or illicit drugs. Blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg and pulse is 130/min and regular. Extremities are cool to the touch with loss of skin turgor. Intravenous access is obtained via 2 large-bore peripheral catheters, and rapid infusion of 2 liters of normal saline is initiated. This intervention is most likely to increase which of the following hemodynamic parameters?

clues.note: Coffee-ground emesis indicates upper GI bleeding (here from peptic ulcer disease), causing blood loss and hypovolemia.

clues.text: Blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg and pulse is 130/min
clues.note: Hypotension with tachycardia (and cool extremities, poor turgor) indicates HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK from blood loss.

clues.text: rapid infusion of 2 liters of normal saline
clues.note: IV isotonic fluids expand intravascular volume, increasing venous return and ventricular filling (PRELOAD).

whatMatters: IV NORMAL SALINE expands intravascular volume in hypovolemic shock, increasing venous return and LV end-diastolic volume (PRELOAD). Increased preload stretches the myocardium, INCREASING END-DIASTOLIC SARCOMERE LENGTH -> greater stroke volume via the Frank-Starling mechanism. Answer C.
strategy: Translate 'fluids increase preload' into the cellular measure: increased end-diastolic volume = increased ventricular filling = increased END-DIASTOLIC SARCOMERE LENGTH (Frank-Starling). Reject parameters that fluids do NOT raise (or actually lower): aortic wall elasticity (fixed structural property), diastolic compliance (intrinsic myocardial property), heart rate (falls as perfusion improves/sympathetic drive decreases), plasma renin activity (decreases with volume repletion), and total peripheral resistance/contraction velocity (high from sympathetic drive, fall with resuscitation).

eliminations.label: Aortic wall elasticity - fixed structural property
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: intrinsic compliance of the aortic media. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a fixed structural property not changed by a fluid bolus. ✅ Correct if: age/atherosclerosis altering aortic stiffness (not acute fluids).

eliminations.label: Diastolic ventricular compliance - intrinsic myocardial property
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: how readily the ventricle fills for a given pressure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: compliance is an intrinsic property (reduced by LVH, HCM, infiltration), not increased by giving fluids. ✅ Correct if: conditions that change myocardial stiffness.

eliminations.label: Heart rate - decreases with resuscitation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: beats per minute. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: adequate fluid resuscitation reduces the compensatory tachycardia (less sympathetic drive), so heart rate falls, not rises. ✅ Correct if: worsening hypovolemia raising heart rate.

eliminations.label: Plasma renin activity - decreases with volume repletion
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: renin release reflecting RAAS activation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: renin is HIGH in hypovolemia and DECREASES after volume is restored, not increased. ✅ Correct if: hypovolemia/hypotension activating RAAS.

eliminations.label: Total peripheral resistance - decreases with resuscitation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: systemic vascular resistance/afterload. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: TPR is elevated by compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction in shock and DECREASES as perfusion is restored. ✅ Correct if: increasing sympathetic vasoconstriction (worsening shock).

eliminations.label: Ventricular contraction velocity - decreases with resuscitation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: myocardial contractility/velocity (inotropy). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is high from catecholamine drive in shock and falls as sympathetic activation decreases with fluids; the primary fluid effect is on preload. ✅ Correct if: an inotrope increasing contractility.

reasoning: The patient is in hypovolemic shock from GI bleeding
IV normal saline expands intravascular volume, increasing venous return
Increased ventricular filling raises end-diastolic volume, stretching the myocardium
-> increased end-diastolic sarcomere length (Frank-Starling); answer C
mechanism: HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK from acute blood loss (upper GI bleeding here) reduces intravascular volume, lowering venous return, ventricular filling, stroke volume, and blood pressure; compensatory SYMPATHETIC activation raises heart rate, contractility, and systemic vascular resistance, and the RAAS is activated (high renin). The key treatment (besides controlling the bleed) is rapid intravenous VOLUME EXPANSION with isotonic crystalloid (NORMAL SALINE) or blood. Infused fluid increases the intravascular and left ventricular END-DIASTOLIC VOLUMES (PRELOAD). By the FRANK-STARLING relationship, greater end-diastolic volume STRETCHES the cardiomyocytes, INCREASING the END-DIASTOLIC SARCOMERE LENGTH; this improves actin-myosin overlap and increases the force of contraction, raising STROKE VOLUME and cardiac output. As perfusion is restored, the compensatory heart rate, TPR, contractility, and renin all DECREASE. Aortic wall elasticity and diastolic compliance are intrinsic properties unchanged by a fluid bolus. Therefore fluids most directly INCREASE end-diastolic sarcomere length.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV > preload/Frank-Starling: IV fluids increase intravascular volume -> increased venous return/end-diastolic volume (preload) -> increased sarcomere length -> increased stroke volume; hypovolemic shock compensations (tachycardia, high TPR, high renin) reverse with resuscitation.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Fluids raise preload (end-diastolic volume) -> increased end-diastolic sarcomere length (Frank-Starling).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on preload, end-diastolic volume, sarcomere length, Frank-Starling, or hypovolemic shock compensation? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Heart rate/TPR/renin/contraction velocity are HIGH in shock and FALL with resuscitation; aortic elasticity/compliance are intrinsic.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: IV fluids increase preload -> increased end-diastolic sarcomere length (Frank-Starling) -> increased stroke volume.

keywords.back: Increased preload/sarcomere length -> increased stroke volume

keywords.front: Effect of resuscitation on those compensations

keywords.back: Intrinsic properties (not changed by a fluid bolus)

firstAid.detail: CV: fluids raise end-diastolic sarcomere length -> more stroke volume.

memoryHook: Fill the tank (saline) and the heart fills more each beat - stretching sarcomeres longer (Frank-Starling), so each squeeze ejects more blood.
